title: Deuteronomy 15: The Year of Release and the Hebrew Servant
body:
Read the chapter → [Deuteronomy 15](/bible/deuteronomy/15)

## Introduction

This session read [Deuteronomy 15](/bible/deuteronomy/15) through 18 with brief exposition. Chapter 15 covers the seventh year of release for the poor, the law of lending and giving to the poor brother, the Hebrew servant who must go out free and well furnished in the seventh year, and the firstling males of the herd and flock sanctified unto the Most High. Chapter 16 covers the feast of the passover, the feast of weeks, and the feast of tabernacles, the three times in the year all males appear before the Most High, judges and just judgment, and the groves and images that are forbidden. Chapter 17 covers the sound sacrifice, the judgment of idolaters, hard controversies determined by the priests and judges, and the election and duty of a king. Chapter 18 covers the priests' and Levites' inheritance and their due, the abominations of the nations to be avoided, the Prophet like unto Moses who must be heard, and the presumptuous prophets who are to die.

**[Deuteronomy 15:1-4](/bible/deuteronomy/15#v1)**

> <sup>[1](/bible/deuteronomy/15#v1)</sup> At the end of every seven years thou shalt make a release.
>
> <sup>[2](/bible/deuteronomy/15#v2)</sup> And this is the manner of the release: Every creditor that lendeth ought unto his neighbour shall release it; he shall not exact it of his neighbour, or of his brother; because it is called the Lord’s release.
>
> <sup>[3](/bible/deuteronomy/15#v3)</sup> Of a foreigner thou mayest exact it again: but that which is thine with thy brother thine hand shall release;
>
> <sup>[4](/bible/deuteronomy/15#v4)</sup> Save when there shall be no poor among you; for the Lord shall greatly bless thee in the land which the Lord thy God giveth thee for an inheritance to possess it:

- At the end of every seven years thou shalt make a release: every creditor that lendeth ought unto his neighbour shall release it, and shall not exact it of his neighbour or of his brother, because it is called the Lord's release.
- Of a foreigner thou mayest exact it again, but that which is thine with thy brother thine hand shall release. The seven year release stands on the sabbath of the land already given in [Leviticus 25](/bible/leviticus/25).

  Precepts:
  - **[Leviticus 25:2-4](/bible/leviticus/25#v2)**
    > <sup>[2](/bible/leviticus/25#v2)</sup> Speak unto the children of Israel, and say unto them, When ye come into the land which I give you, then shall the land keep a sabbath unto the Lord.
    >
    > <sup>[3](/bible/leviticus/25#v3)</sup> Six years thou shalt sow thy field, and six years thou shalt prune thy vineyard, and gather in the fruit thereof;
    >
    > <sup>[4](/bible/leviticus/25#v4)</sup> But in the seventh year shall be a sabbath of rest unto the land, a sabbath for the Lord: thou shalt neither sow thy field, nor prune thy vineyard.

    The land keeps a sabbath unto the Lord: six years thou shalt sow thy field, but in the seventh year is a sabbath of rest unto the land.

**[Deuteronomy 15:5-6](/bible/deuteronomy/15#v5)**

> <sup>[5](/bible/deuteronomy/15#v5)</sup> Only if thou carefully hearken unto the voice of the Lord thy God, to observe to do all these commandments which I command thee this day.
>
> <sup>[6](/bible/deuteronomy/15#v6)</sup> For the Lord thy God blesseth thee, as he promised thee: and thou shalt lend unto many nations, but thou shalt not borrow; and thou shalt reign over many nations, but they shall not reign over thee.

- If thou carefully hearken unto the voice of the Most High to observe all these commandments, thou shalt lend unto many nations but thou shalt not borrow, and thou shalt reign over many nations but they shall not reign over thee.
- This is the blessing that was to come upon us. Since we broke the commandments of the Most High, the other nations lend to us and we borrow from them; we go to them for loans and everything else.

  Precepts:
  - **[Deuteronomy 28:12](/bible/deuteronomy/28#v12)**
    > <sup>[12](/bible/deuteronomy/28#v12)</sup> The Lord shall open unto thee his good treasure, the heaven to give the rain unto thy land in his season, and to bless all the work of thine hand: and thou shalt lend unto many nations, and thou shalt not borrow.

    The Lord shall open unto thee his good treasure, and thou shalt lend unto many nations and shalt not borrow; the blessing Israel forfeited by breaking the commandments.

**[Deuteronomy 15:7-8](/bible/deuteronomy/15#v7)**

> <sup>[7](/bible/deuteronomy/15#v7)</sup> If there be among you a poor man of one of thy brethren within any of thy gates in thy land which the Lord thy God giveth thee, thou shalt not harden thine heart, nor shut thine hand from thy poor brother:
>
> <sup>[8](/bible/deuteronomy/15#v8)</sup> But thou shalt open thine hand wide unto him, and shalt surely lend him sufficient for his need, in that which he wanteth.

- If there be among you a poor man of one of thy brethren, thou shalt not harden thine heart nor shut thine hand from thy poor brother.
- It is a commandment to us to help our brothers: open thine hand wide unto him and lend him sufficient for his need, in that which he wanteth.

**[Deuteronomy 15:9-11](/bible/deuteronomy/15#v9)**

> <sup>[9](/bible/deuteronomy/15#v9)</sup> Beware that there be not a thought in thy wicked heart, saying, The seventh year, the year of release, is at hand; and thine eye be evil against thy poor brother, and thou givest him nought; and he cry unto the Lord against thee, and it be sin unto thee.
>
> <sup>[10](/bible/deuteronomy/15#v10)</sup> Thou shalt surely give him, and thine heart shall not be grieved when thou givest unto him: because that for this thing the Lord thy God shall bless thee in all thy works, and in all that thou puttest thine hand unto.
>
> <sup>[11](/bible/deuteronomy/15#v11)</sup> For the poor shall never cease out of the land: therefore I command thee, saying, Thou shalt open thine hand wide unto thy brother, to thy poor, and to thy needy, in thy land.

- Beware that there be not a thought in thy wicked heart saying, The seventh year, the year of release, is at hand, and thine eye be evil against thy poor brother and thou givest him nought; if he cry unto the Lord against thee, it is sin unto thee.
- Give him surely, and let not thine heart be grieved when thou givest, for because of this thing the Most High shall bless thee in all thy works.
- Notice that Esau had this Bible, these commandments and these laws, yet worked us to death for over four hundred years, and when they released us we did not go out with anything. They had these laws written before them and did not do them.
- The poor shall never cease out of the land; Christ said the same, that the poor are always going to be among us. That is why no campaign can fight poverty out of existence: Christ said it will always be among us.

  Precepts:
  - **[Matthew 26:11](/bible/matthew/26#v11)**
    > <sup>[11](/bible/matthew/26#v11)</sup> For ye have the poor always with you; but me ye have not always.

    Ye have the poor always with you; poverty does not cease, so the commandment is to open thine hand to thy poor brother.

**[Deuteronomy 15:12-15](/bible/deuteronomy/15#v12)**

> <sup>[12](/bible/deuteronomy/15#v12)</sup> And if thy brother, an Hebrew man, or an Hebrew woman, be sold unto thee, and serve thee six years; then in the seventh year thou shalt let him go free from thee.
>
> <sup>[13](/bible/deuteronomy/15#v13)</sup> And when thou sendest him out free from thee, thou shalt not let him go away empty:
>
> <sup>[14](/bible/deuteronomy/15#v14)</sup> Thou shalt furnish him liberally out of thy flock, and out of thy floor, and out of thy winepress: of that wherewith the Lord thy God hath blessed thee thou shalt give unto him.
>
> <sup>[15](/bible/deuteronomy/15#v15)</sup> And thou shalt remember that thou wast a bondman in the land of Egypt, and the Lord thy God redeemed thee: therefore I command thee this thing to day.

- If thy brother, an Hebrew man or an Hebrew woman, be sold unto thee and serve thee six years, then in the seventh year thou shalt let him go free, and thou shalt not let him go away empty.
- When people say slavery was taking place in Africa among us, it was not slavery like we suffered: it was people among us that fell poor and sold themselves to their brothers, the very case this law and [Leviticus 25](/bible/leviticus/25) govern.
- Thou shalt furnish him liberally out of thy flock, out of thy floor, and out of thy winepress; he must leave blessed, with some of the flock, the corn, and the wine. He cannot go out poor the way he came in; that shows you the Most High is a good God.
- The reason given is memory: remember that thou wast a bondman in the land of Egypt, and the Lord thy God redeemed thee.

  Precepts:
  - **[Leviticus 25:39](/bible/leviticus/25#v39)**
    > <sup>[39](/bible/leviticus/25#v39)</sup> And if thy brother that dwelleth by thee be waxen poor, and be sold unto thee; thou shalt not compel him to serve as a bondservant:

    If thy brother that dwelleth by thee be waxen poor and be sold unto thee; the Hebrew sold himself to his brother when he fell poor.

**[Deuteronomy 15:16-18](/bible/deuteronomy/15#v16)**

> <sup>[16](/bible/deuteronomy/15#v16)</sup> And it shall be, if he say unto thee, I will not go away from thee; because he loveth thee and thine house, because he is well with thee;
>
> <sup>[17](/bible/deuteronomy/15#v17)</sup> Then thou shalt take an aul, and thrust it through his ear unto the door, and he shall be thy servant for ever. And also unto thy maidservant thou shalt do likewise.
>
> <sup>[18](/bible/deuteronomy/15#v18)</sup> It shall not seem hard unto thee, when thou sendest him away free from thee; for he hath been worth a double hired servant to thee, in serving thee six years: and the Lord thy God shall bless thee in all that thou doest.

- If the servant say, I will not go away from thee, because he loveth thee and thine house and is well with thee, then thou shalt take an aul and thrust it through his ear unto the door, and he shall be thy servant for ever; likewise unto thy maidservant.
- It shall not seem hard unto thee when thou sendest him away free, for he hath been worth a double hired servant to thee in serving thee six years.
- A double hired servant: reading this makes you think about slavery and how many years they had us. We were double hired servants unto them, and we still serve them even to this day.

**[Deuteronomy 15:19-23](/bible/deuteronomy/15#v19)**

> <sup>[19](/bible/deuteronomy/15#v19)</sup> All the firstling males that come of thy herd and of thy flock thou shalt sanctify unto the Lord thy God: thou shalt do no work with the firstling of thy bullock, nor shear the firstling of thy sheep.
>
> <sup>[20](/bible/deuteronomy/15#v20)</sup> Thou shalt eat it before the Lord thy God year by year in the place which the Lord shall choose, thou and thy household.
>
> <sup>[21](/bible/deuteronomy/15#v21)</sup> And if there be any blemish therein, as if it be lame, or blind, or have any ill blemish, thou shalt not sacrifice it unto the Lord thy God.
>
> <sup>[22](/bible/deuteronomy/15#v22)</sup> Thou shalt eat it within thy gates: the unclean and the clean person shall eat it alike, as the roebuck, and as the hart.
>
> <sup>[23](/bible/deuteronomy/15#v23)</sup> Only thou shalt not eat the blood thereof; thou shalt pour it upon the ground as water.

- All the firstling males of thy herd and of thy flock thou shalt sanctify unto the Most High: thou shalt do no work with the firstling of thy bullock, nor shear the firstling of thy sheep.
- The firstlings were to do no work at all; they were to be sacrificed to the Most High, and thou shalt eat it before the Lord thy God year by year in the place which the Lord shall choose.
- If there be any blemish therein, as if it be lame or blind, thou shalt not sacrifice it unto the Lord thy God; thou shalt eat it within thy gates, the unclean and the clean person alike, as the roebuck and as the hart.
- Only thou shalt not eat the blood thereof; thou shalt pour it upon the ground as water.
